RESULTS

Equity gains are tunable—and dataset dependent

The method exposes a controllable trade-off: stronger equity can reduce imbalance, but the cost and solver context matter.

Tune the equity weight
Increasing β and γ produces larger CV reductions, alongside larger cost increases.
The pattern travels across classes
Across clustered, random, and random-clustered Solomon classes, HERO reduces CV.
Asymmetry reveals the limit
Against cost-only ALNS, HERO lowers CV but carries a larger increase in total cost.
A trade-off, not a free lunch
